title: The model method: bar models for word problems
subject: math
strengths: Most of the class can draw unit boxes that are all the same length and line the bars up to compare them.
The class can use a before-and-after model to show what changed and a part-whole model to find a difference.

modelAnswers.question: Mia has 3 units. She gives 1 unit away to her sister. Draw a before-and-after model in your head: how many units does Mia have left?
A class bar is split into 7 equal units. 3 units are boys and the rest are girls. How many units are girls, and what is the difference between the girls' units and the boys' units?

commonErrors.misconception: Drawing unit boxes in any lengths, guessing the sizes.
commonErrors.example: A learner draws Sam's 2-unit bar only a little longer than the 1-unit bar on the worksheet, treating the bar as a rough sketch.

fixIt.prompt: Fix it: measure each unit box against the first one - how long should the 2-unit bar be compared with the 1-unit bar?
fixIt.corrected: Corrected working: every unit box is exactly the same length, so the 2-unit bar is exactly twice the 1-unit bar.

commonErrors.misconception: Drawing unit boxes in any lengths, guessing the sizes.
commonErrors.example: On the exit ticket, a learner defends the guessed lengths by saying a bar model is only a rough sketch.

fixIt.prompt: Fix it: say what makes a bar model trustworthy - then redraw the 1-unit and 2-unit bars with matching unit boxes.
fixIt.corrected: Corrected check: the bar is a scale model, not a rough sketch, so two units is exactly twice one unit.

nextSteps: Reteach unit boxes as equal parts, landing the ruler check that every box matches, before any further model questions.
Practise drawing the whole bar first and splitting it into equal units before marking the parts.
